controls.detail: The simulator reports a brightness value but has no writable physical backlight.
This device has no rear torch.
Use the native volume panel. iOS does not provide a general writable system volume property.
Choose an available output in the system route picker.
The native route picker chooses compatible audio/video destinations for the app; it does not enable system screen mirroring.
Low Power Mode is observed from iOS. Change it in the system Settings app.

snapshot.detail: Public UIKit device integrations. Contacts respect the selected access scope; message composition reports the actual system composer outcome. Device controls reflect observed hardware and permissions.

roles.detail: The running device/build does not have an eligible signed Default Dialer entitlement. The standard calling handoff remains available.
Carrier messaging requires the signed entitlement, an eligible iPhone/region and selection as default. The normal message composer remains separate.

independent_artifact_reverification.method: Reapplied the actual verify-ios-smoke.py and verify-ios-devices.py contracts to the downloaded originals, also requiring each native observation to be later than its preserved URL request and the XCTest handler to report the same ordered six system opens.

visual_review.summary: Start and restored Start render live tiles; Wallet renders its empty-state controls; Phone contains the exact URL-provided number without calling; People renders simulator-native contacts; Messaging renders its draft fields; Settings renders the device-services child page. Each measured surface is contained within the native safe area.

warnings: Native compilation retained unused-parameter/deprecation warnings and upstream Rust warnings; both complete configurations linked and bundled successfully. Full diagnostics are retained in the job log.
The runtime emitted FerroUI keyless-list warnings; all independently checked mounted route and geometry assertions passed.
The simulator cannot open tel:0 and reported no carrier roles, phone accounts or messaging transport. This is preserved as unsupported observed capability.
XCTest logged an Apple simulator accessibility class duplication warning; its actual test completed with zero failures.

prior_causal_corrections.change: Report simulator brightness as read-only and reject writes; retain physical-device writable support. Native Contacts CRUD stays required.
Use the public XCTest system URL API with exact ordered URI requests, independent native delegate outcomes, unchanged process identity and foreground-scene assertions.
Batch shared launch/activation delivery and accept the final route owned by the requested app, preserving Settings child redirects and session/epoch ownership.
Add opt-in early Rust/UIKit setup phases and prelaunch installation identity for bounded owned-process/crash diagnostics; production providers and runtime assertions are unchanged.

limitations: This qualifies an ARM64 iOS simulator build/runtime. Physical iPhone call, carrier SMS/MMS, entitled role selection, regional eligibility, and hardware brightness/torch behavior require separate device qualification.

The optional carrier provider was physically targeted Swift-typechecked and fully linked into the simulator bundle. No signed carrier entitlement, provisioning profile, role selection or live cellular service was installed or claimed.
The test placed no calls and sent no messages. Phone and Messaging captures establish actual native activation and mounted UI, not successful telephony or MessageUI transmission.
Simulator contacts shown in People are disposable simulator fixtures. Existing Start demo badges do not establish carrier inbox synchronization on iOS.
URL delivery, Contacts CRUD and measured safe-area behavior are runtime-qualified; every other native integration retains its documented device-specific qualification limits.
